false_positives.candidate:
Attribute-keys query key omits the organization

`queryKey` is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` only contains item type, attribute type, project ids and the datetime range — the organization slug used to build the request URL is not part of the key. Two organizations with the same project ids/date range would share a cache entry, so attribute keys from one org can be served for another after an org switch within the same session. Include the organization slug (or the full URL) in the query key.

Coverage for the application/reports+json content type was removed

The previous test posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"` (the content type browsers actually use for the Reporting API) and asserted the request body was logged. After the refactor every success-path test posts with the default content type, so `BrowserReportsJSONParser` — the only reason the custom parser class exists — is no longer exercised by any test. A regression in the parser media type would silently break real browser reports while the suite stays green.

Custom cell renderers fall back on any falsy return, not just undefined

Both `renderDefaultHeadCell` and `renderDefaultBodyCell` do `const cell = render...(); if (cell) return cell;`. The documented contract (see tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx and the prop JSDoc) is that returning `undefined` triggers the fallback renderer. With a truthiness check, a custom renderer that legitimately returns `null` (render nothing), `''`, or `0` will be silently replaced by the default renderer, which is not what the docs promise and is hard to debug. Compare against `undefined` explicitly.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter only applies while searching

`sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `searchQuery` is empty, so the newly added `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` exclusion (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is only applied once the user types something. In the default (no search) state those attributes are still shown, which is the opposite of the intent and makes the list inconsistent as soon as a user starts/clears a search. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied to the base list, independently of the search term.

Hook can now return undefined attributes where it previously always returned a TagCollection

The hook was rewritten to return `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data` from `useQuery`. `data` is `undefined` whenever the query errors, is disabled (`enabled` false), or has not run, and `previous` is also `undefined` on the first render — whereas the old implementation always derived a concrete `TagCollection` object (`result.data ?? []` reduced into `{}`). Consumers that do `Object.keys(attributes)` or spread the value (e.g. the filter-key sections / search query builder tag collections) will throw on error or while the hook is disabled. Default to `{}` (or make the undefined case explicit for all callers).

One invalid report rejects the entire batch

The POST handler returns 422 for the whole request as soon as any single report in the array fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same batch. Browsers send reports in batches and will keep retrying the same (permanently invalid) payload, so a single malformed report from one page permanently blocks collection of the rest of that batch. Consider skipping/counting invalid reports and still returning 200 for the valid ones.

get_environment_info triggers a per-issue recommended-event lookup during PR comment generation

`get_environment_info()` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment. That helper performs a search/snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per issue, so generating a comment for the top 5 issues now issues up to 5 extra remote queries inside the webhook/task path that previously only read `issue.culprit` from the already-loaded model. This adds latency and external load to every PR comment, and the broad `except Exception` means failures are invisible apart from an info log. Consider batching the environment lookup (or deriving it from data already fetched for the issue list).

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup codes are matched case-sensitively and without trimming

`backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` only strips dashes. The generated codes are lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), but users typically retype them from a printout and mobile keyboards auto-capitalise the first character, and copy/paste frequently adds surrounding whitespace. Any uppercase character or stray space makes a valid code be rejected with `IncorrectBackupCode`, consuming the user's rate-limit budget and potentially locking them out of the very recovery path this feature adds. Normalise with `.trim().toLowerCase()` (same issue exists in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` line 61).

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write

The code decrypts `user.backupCodes`, nulls out the matched entry in memory and then writes the whole re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. Two requests that arrive concurrently both read the same pre-update array, so (a) the same backup code can be redeemed more than once (breaking the 'each code can be used exactly once' guarantee stated in `backup_code_instructions`), and (b) if two different codes are redeemed concurrently the second write resurrects the code invalidated by the first. Consuming the code needs to be atomic (e.g. a conditional/compare-and-set update inside a transaction, or storing codes in their own rows and deleting by unique key).

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
resetState() leaves backup codes in memory and leaks the blob URL

`resetState()` clears only `password`, `errorMessage` and `step`; `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri` and `secret` persist. The `URL.createObjectURL` blob is only revoked on the next successful `handleSetup` call, so closing the dialog (or navigating away) leaks the object URL for the page's lifetime, and the plaintext recovery codes stay in component state after the dialog is closed. Revoke the URL and clear the code state in `resetState()`/on unmount.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

false_positives.candidate:
Assertion is a no-op and the new backup-code auth paths are untested

`expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the returned Promise, which is always truthy, so this step passes even when 2FA was not enabled — the PR adds a FIXME comment acknowledging this but leaves the broken assertion in place (use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or the `data-state="checked"` selector as the second test does). In addition, the only new coverage is clicking download/copy/close on the backup-code screen; the actual security-relevant paths added by this PR — logging in with a backup code, single-use invalidation of a redeemed code, and disabling 2FA with a backup code — have no tests at all (only a TODO), which is how issues like the password-bypass and case-sensitivity problems go unnoticed.

Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed

`backupCodes` is persisted as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, so anyone who obtains a database dump plus the (usually env-deployed, long-lived) `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` recovers every user's usable recovery credentials in plaintext. Unlike `twoFactorSecret`, backup codes never need to be displayed again after setup — only compared — so they should be stored as one-way hashes (e.g. per-code hash, compared by hashing the submitted code) to limit the impact of a DB/key compromise.

Backup-code login path lets a caller skip password verification entirely

Password verification only runs in the block at line 121 (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`), i.e. it is skipped whenever a non-empty `totpCode` is submitted. The new backup-code branch at line 131 (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`) takes precedence over the TOTP branch, so a request that sends a dummy non-empty `totpCode` together with a valid `backupCode` has neither its password nor its TOTP code verified: the password check is skipped because `totpCode` is set, and the TOTP check is skipped because the backup-code branch ran instead. The result is that possession of a single backup code (e.g. from the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt`) is enough to sign in with just the e-mail address, downgrading 2FA from 'second factor' to 'only factor'. The branch should require that the password was actually verified (or verify it explicitly) before accepting a backup code.

Submitting an empty backup code silently does nothing

`BackupCode.tsx` relies on the HTML `required`/`minLength` attributes, but the login form is rendered with `noValidate` and the zod schema only validates `email`/`password` (`.passthrough()` for everything else), so an empty backup code is submitted. Server-side an empty `backupCode` is falsy, so the TOTP branch runs and returns `ErrorCode.SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` and shows no message at all. From the user's point of view pressing Submit on the 'Lost access' screen does nothing — no error, no feedback. Validate `backupCode` in the form schema (or map `SecondFactorRequired` to a visible error while in lost-access mode).

Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint

`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` is called on whatever JSON the client sent. A non-string value (e.g. `{"backupCode": 1234567890}` or an array) makes `replaceAll` throw a TypeError that is not caught, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Similarly `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` at line 58 throws if the stored blob cannot be decrypted/parsed. Validate the body (zod/typeof check) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch returning a proper error code.

onEnable() is only invoked by the Close button, so dismissing the backup-code dialog leaves the parent UI stale

Previously `onEnable()` was called as soon as the enable request succeeded (old line 135). Now success only advances to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, and `onEnable()` is called exclusively from the `backup-codes-close` button handler. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (the Dialog's close/X control, Escape, clicking the overlay — all of which go through `onOpenChange`), 2FA is enabled server-side but the parent never runs its `onEnable` callback, so the two-factor switch / cached query is not refreshed and the settings page reports 2FA as disabled until a manual reload. `onEnable()` should also be fired when the dialog closes from the DisplayBackupCodes step.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unguarded access to first destinationCalendar crashes Google Meet fallback

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar (empty array or null, which is now a very common case — several call sites build `destinationCalendar: []`). The very next line dereferences it: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. For any booking whose location is Google Meet and whose organizer/event type has no destination calendar, this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the whole booking creation fails. Use optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`).

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent destination-calendar fallback can never match

`const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined/""` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Result: for bookings whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, and references created by `updateLocation`, see above), `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined`, so the Google request is malformed and the update fails instead of hitting the host's destination calendar. Should fall back to the first destination calendar's `externalId`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition inverted (unrelated change)

`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the condition. With team billing enabled the org now gets both a real `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` (the requestedSlug flow exists precisely because the slug must not be claimed until payment), and with billing disabled (self-hosted default) the organization is created with no slug at all, so org subdomain resolution breaks. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be reverted.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateAllCalendarEvents can call updateEvent with an undefined credential

Inside the new per-reference loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set but neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB lookup yields a usable credential (e.g. credential deleted, or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` missing), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is still pushed. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` dereferences `credential.appName`/`credential.type` when building its result, throwing a TypeError. Because `return Promise.all(result)` is not awaited inside the `try`, that rejection escapes the surrounding try/catch and surfaces as an unhandled rejection rather than the intended degraded result. Skip the reference when no credential could be resolved.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when there is no primary destination calendar

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and the collective handling is `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With optional chaining on `null`, the push is a no-op, so for a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but other hosts do, none of the host calendars are used — exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialise the field to an array (or assign the collected list) instead of relying on `?.push`.

Credential-less destinations create events in every credential of that integration

For each destination without a `credentialId`, the code creates an event in every calendar credential of the matching integration type (`this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)`). Now that `destinationCalendar` is an array and is populated with each collective host's calendar, two hosts with credential-less Google destination calendars cause 2 × (number of google credentials) event creations, i.e. duplicate calendar entries for the same booking. Additionally the resulting `EventResult`s carry no `externalId`, so the persisted booking references lose the external calendar id. De-duplicate destinations and pass the destination's `externalId` through.

Error diagnostics removed from updateAllCalendarEvents catch block

The catch block still computes the detailed `message` string but the `console.error(message)` call was deleted, so `message` is now dead code and calendar update failures are swallowed completely with no log output. Debugging multi-host calendar failures (the exact scenario this PR targets) becomes impossible; keep a log statement.

Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId

`selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (when no destination calendar matches `credentialId`); the insert call guards this with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the Meet link into the description does not. When `selectedCalendar` is undefined the patch request is malformed and the event description will be missing the hangout link. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value for the patch.

Invalid dynamicUserList surfaces as a 500 instead of 400

`throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is thrown inside the new `try` in `loadUsers`, but the catch only maps `HttpError` and Prisma errors to a 400; everything else becomes `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed client request (empty dynamic user list) is therefore reported as a server error and the actual reason is lost. Throw an `HttpError` with status 400 directly.

No tests for the array-based destinationCalendar behaviour

This PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across ~20 files and adds new branching in `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` (per-destination credential resolution, DB credential fallback, collective host aggregation), yet no unit/integration tests were added and the only test touched is an e2e expectation value. Given the number of null/empty-array edge cases introduced (see the Google Meet crash and the dropped collective calendars), at least tests covering: empty destinationCalendar, destination without credentialId, and a collective event with two hosts, are needed before merge.

Recurring cancellation now issues duplicated delete calls per calendar reference

The recurring branch (iterate all of the user's calendar credentials × all `updatedBookings`' first calendar reference) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references on a booking the whole credential×booking deletion matrix is executed N times, sending the same `deleteEvent` request repeatedly to each provider (and pushing N× duplicate promises into `apiDeletes`). For multi-host collective recurring events this multiplies external API calls and the risk of rate limiting. Hoist the recurring handling out of the per-reference loop.

Video booking references no longer store credentialId

In `create()`, `referencesToCreate` now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously the non-calendar branch used `result.credentialId`, i.e. the video credential id returned by `createMeeting`. With this change every `_video` booking reference is persisted with `credentialId = null`. Cancellation code (`handleCancelBooking`: `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`) only deletes the meeting when that id is present, so video meetings will silently never be deleted on cancellation for all new bookings.

createEvent now ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId

The target calendar is resolved exclusively via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable and is null for rows created before credential linking, so for those users the event is now written to `"primary"` instead of their configured destination calendar — a behaviour regression from the previous `destinationCalendar.externalId` lookup. Worse, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` still records `externalId: destination.externalId` in the booking reference for the credential-ful branch, so the stored reference can disagree with the calendar actually used, breaking later update/delete.

deleteEvent destination-calendar fallback can never match

Same inverted predicate as in `updateEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always resolves to `undefined` and `calendarId` degrades to `"primary"`. Events that live in a non-primary destination calendar and whose booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId` will no longer be deleted (Google returns 404, which the handler swallows), leaving orphaned calendar entries.

organization relation removed from the dynamic-booking user select

In the `!eventTypeId` (dynamic group booking) branch of `loadUsers`, the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` sub-select was dropped. Any downstream consumer of `user.organization` for dynamic bookings (e.g. building org-scoped booker URLs) will now see `undefined`, and the two branches of `loadUsers` return structurally different user shapes, which weakens the inferred type the comment claims to rely on. Re-add the select unless you have verified no consumer reads it.

updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId

`updateLocation()` builds `referencesToCreate` from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but these results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent()`, which never sets `externalId` or `credentialId` on its returned `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). Both fields are therefore always `undefined`, whereas the previous code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `.credentialId`. The references written by `editLocation.handler.ts` will have no external calendar id or credential id, so subsequent updates/deletes of that booking will target the credential-less legacy path / the "primary" calendar instead of the real destination calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"

When the refreshed-token response has no `refresh_token`, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This placeholder is then persisted into the credential key by callers (e.g. office365calendar, zoomvideo, salesforce). On the next refresh the provider is called with the bogus value `"refresh_token"`, which fails with invalid_grant and can mark the credential invalid — overwriting a previously valid refresh token with garbage. If the intent is "keep the existing refresh token", it must copy the old value from the stored credential instead of inventing a string.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to "[object Object]"

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property names; a Zod schema object has no meaningful `toString()`, so both evaluate to the same literal key `"[object Object]"` and the second declaration overwrites the first. The effective schema is therefore `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Because Zod strips unknown keys by default, parsing a sync-endpoint response drops `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`refresh_token` and everything else. Consumers (office365calendar, zoomvideo, salesforce) then persist a credential key containing only `access_token`, so the token is treated as permanently expired (or fails later schema validation) and a refresh is triggered on every call. The intent ("allow any extra properties, assume a numeric property is the expiry") needs `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` or `.catchall()`.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with a zod SafeParse result object

`parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed object, yet the result is stored directly: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the credential object. After the first token refresh the DB row becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor throws and the user's Google Calendar integration breaks permanently (requires reconnect). Either return `.data` from the helper or use `...data` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential-sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect app-specific shapes

When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `Response` of the POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, but several callers pass a `refreshFunction` whose return type is not a `Response`: hubspot's `tokensApi.createToken()` returns a token object and the caller reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` / `.accessToken`; zoho-bigin and zohocrm use axios and read `tokenInfo.data`; googlecalendar reads `res?.data`. With sync enabled these all read `undefined` off a `Response`, producing `NaN` expiry dates, `setAccessToken(undefined)` and corrupted credential rows instead of a working token. The helper needs to normalise the sync response to the same shape each caller expects (or each caller must branch explicitly).

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential-sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect app-specific shapes

When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `Response` of the POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, but several callers pass a `refreshFunction` whose return type is not a `Response`: hubspot's `tokensApi.createToken()` returns a token object and the caller reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` / `.accessToken`; zoho-bigin and zohocrm use axios and read `tokenInfo.data`; googlecalendar reads `res?.data`. With sync enabled these all read `undefined` off a `Response`, producing `NaN` expiry dates, `setAccessToken(undefined)` and corrupted credential rows instead of a working token. The helper needs to normalise the sync response to the same shape each caller expects (or each caller must branch explicitly).

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId

`refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` – the third argument of the helper is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Passing the credential id means the self-hosted endpoint is asked to refresh tokens for an unrelated (or non-existent) user, which at best fails and at worst returns another user's access token. `refreshAccessToken` only receives `credentialId`/`credentialKey`, so the credential's `userId` must be threaded through.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce refresh failure check relies on `response.statusText === "OK"`

`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText })`. `statusText` is not guaranteed: HTTP/2 responses (which Salesforce serves) have an empty `statusText`, so a perfectly successful 200 response is rejected with an empty error message, and conversely error bodies are reported without any detail. Use `response.ok` / `response.status` and include the response body in the error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce now performs an unconditional token refresh on every service instantiation, and discards the new token

`getClient()` unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` each time a `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed — there is no expiry check as in the other apps. This burns Salesforce OAuth rate limits (and adds latency) on every booking operation. Worse, the refreshed token is written to the DB but the `jsforce.Connection` below is still created with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` (the old token), so the refresh has no effect on the current request and an expired credential still fails.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook does not restrict HTTP method and crashes with 500 on malformed input

The handler accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without try/catch. A bad body, a wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext throws out of the handler, returning an unhandled 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with a useful message. Validate the method (POST only) and wrap parse/decrypt in error handling that returns 400.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or token-parsing helpers

The PR adds a publicly reachable endpoint that writes third-party OAuth credentials into the database plus two shared helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) used by ~10 app integrations, with no unit or integration tests. Given the defects that are easy to introduce here (secret verification, decryption, schema shape, which branch of the helper is taken), tests covering: disabled sharing → 403, wrong secret → 403, unknown user/app → 404, create vs. update path, and the minimum-token-response parsing would prevent regressions in all app refresh flows.

Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication and its status is not checked

The POST to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature or bearer token, so the endpoint handing out OAuth access tokens cannot verify that the caller is Cal.com and effectively has to be an unauthenticated public endpoint. (The inbound webhook does verify `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the outbound call should do the equivalent.) The response status is also never checked, so a 4xx/5xx body is passed downstream and parsed as if it were a token.

Updating a synced credential does not clear the `invalid` flag

When an existing credential is found, only `key` is updated. If the credential had previously been marked `invalid: true` (which Cal.com does on invalid_grant, e.g. in googlecalendar/zoom/webex), pushing fresh working keys leaves `invalid` set, so the credential continues to be treated as broken and the app stays unusable for the user. The update should also reset `invalid: false`.

Webex refresh still validates with the strict schema, so credential sync responses are rejected

Webex was switched to `refreshOAuthTokens` but still parses the result with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)`, which requires `scope` to equal the exact literal `"spark:kms meeting:schedules_read meeting:schedules_write"`, plus `token_type`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. The documented sync-endpoint contract is "only the access token and expiry date", so with credential sharing enabled every Webex refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". It should go through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` like zoom/office365/salesforce.

Webhook secret compared with `!==` (timing-unsafe) and header lookup is case-sensitive

The shared secret is compared with a plain string inequality, which leaks information through timing; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Additionally `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME]` relies on the operator setting the header name in lowercase (Node lowercases incoming header keys); if an uppercase name is configured the lookup silently returns `undefined` and every request is rejected with "Invalid webhook secret". Lowercase the configured name before the lookup.

Zoom sends appSlug "zoomvideo" which is not the app's slug

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but the Zoom app's slug (used for `appId` in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` and looked up by the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint) is `zoom`. A self-hoster keying their sync endpoint off the slug they receive from the webhook will not match the slug sent on refresh, so Zoom token refresh via credential sync silently fails. Other apps in this PR pass real slugs (e.g. `msteams`, `google-calendar`), so this is an inconsistency, not a convention.

`prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService

`prisma.credential.update(...)` is called inside `getClient()` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (imports are only getLocation, WEBAPP_URL, HttpError, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug, parseRefreshTokenResponse). This will fail type-check/build, and at runtime throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce calendar operation, making the Salesforce app completely unusable.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees

`blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased, but the incoming `guest` string is never normalized, so `Blocked@Example.com` passes the blacklist filter while `blocked@example.com` would be blocked. The duplicate check `attendee.email === guest` is likewise case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added again with different casing, creating a second attendee row and duplicate emails for the same person. Normalize (trim + lowercase) guest emails before both checks and before persisting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team permission check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both an admin *and* the owner. Despite the variable name, a team ADMIN who is not the owner will be denied, and the combined condition is effectively "is owner" only. This should be an OR (or a single role check). Consequence: team admins who are legitimately allowed to manage team bookings cannot add guests. It also issues two extra DB queries with `teamId ?? 0` for personal bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the actually-added guests

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input array. In `email-manager.sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in this array decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new-booking style) or the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification. Any email the caller submitted that was filtered out because it is already an attendee therefore receives a brand-new "booking confirmed" email instead of the "guests added" notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Input guest list is not de-duplicated server-side

The filter only removes guests that already exist as attendees or are blacklisted; it does not de-duplicate the `guests` array itself. The client dialog enforces uniqueness, but the tRPC endpoint is callable directly, so `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` creates two attendee rows for the same email on the booking, which then receive duplicate emails and show up twice in the booking UI and calendar event. De-duplicate (e.g. via a Set) before `createMany`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings

Every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`) takes an `eventTypeMetadata` argument and guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members and all attendees, so event types configured with standard host/attendee emails disabled will still send mail, breaking that setting.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Attendees are created without seat references for seated event types

For event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, every attendee is normally paired with a `BookingSeat` record (seatsReferences). This handler inserts attendees directly via `attendees.createMany` with no seat reference and without checking remaining seat capacity, so seated bookings end up with attendees that have no seat uid. Those guests cannot cancel/reschedule via the seat flow and the booking can exceed its configured seat count.

Calendar/video update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's

`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the session user, while `evt.destinationCalendar` is derived from the booking's organizer/destination calendar. When a team admin/owner or an attendee (both allowed by the permission check above) adds guests, the handler will try to update the organizer's calendar event with the wrong account's credentials, so `updateCalendarAttendees` silently fails or targets an unrelated calendar and the external event is never updated with the new guests. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials`, already fetched) should be used.

Component inside packages/ui imports from its own barrel (@calcom/ui), creating a circular dependency

`import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` imports the package's own entry point (`packages/ui/index.tsx`), which in turn re-exports this very module via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`. Sibling components in this folder import their dependencies by relative path for this reason. The cycle can produce undefined imports at runtime (especially combined with the `next/dynamic` lazy wrapper) and pulls the whole UI barrel into the lazily-loaded chunk, defeating the purpose of `MultiEmailLazy`. Use relative imports (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, etc.).

Email failure is swallowed without logging the error

`catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and uses `console.log` rather than the project `logger`. If sending fails (bad SMTP config, template error) there is no stack trace or context (bookingId, guests) to debug with, and the mutation still reports success to the user.

Error toast exposes raw tRPC code and the fallback message is dead code

`const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never fall back; when `err.data` is missing the user sees `undefined: ...`. The toast also surfaces an internal error code plus an un-translated server message key to end users. Prefer translating the known message keys and falling back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when the key is unknown.

Hardcoded English tooltip text in shared UI component

`<Tooltip content="Remove email">` uses a hardcoded English string in a shared, user-facing component while the rest of the component uses `t(...)`. Non-English users will see untranslated text; the string should come from the locale files.

New mutation with non-trivial authorization logic has no tests

`addGuestsHandler` introduces an authorization matrix (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), blacklist filtering, duplicate filtering, attendee persistence, calendar update and email dispatch, but the PR adds no unit or integration tests. Given the permission bug (AND instead of OR), the case-sensitivity bypass and the credential mix-up noted elsewhere in this review, tests covering at least the authorization branches and the filtering of duplicates/blacklisted emails are needed before merge.

No upper bound on the number of guests accepted

`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` constraint. Any authenticated user who is an attendee or organizer of a booking can submit an arbitrarily long list of arbitrary email addresses; each one is persisted as an attendee and receives an email from the Cal.com mail server. This is a mail-amplification/spam vector and an unbounded DB write. Add a reasonable maximum (and a minimum of 1) to the schema.

No validation of booking status; guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings

The handler only checks existence and permissions. It never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`, so a caller can add guests to a CANCELLED/REJECTED booking or to one that already ended; in each case new attendee rows are created and "guests added" emails with a CONFIRMED ICS (`status: "CONFIRMED"`, `method: "REQUEST"`) are sent out, which can re-create a cancelled event on recipients' calendars. The UI also surfaces this action for past bookings (editBookingActions is rendered for past/confirmed bookings), so the server must reject these cases.

Validation error state is never cleared except via Cancel

`setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is only reset in the Cancel button handler. If the user fixes the invalid/duplicate emails and submits successfully, or closes the dialog with the X/overlay and reopens it, the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message remains visible. Reset the flag at the start of `handleAdd` and when the dialog opens/closes.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount updated with a read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment

Both update calls set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (cron overrun, manual trigger, or a retrying scheduler), both read the same `retryCount` and write the same value, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can be retried indefinitely — exactly the loop this PR is trying to stop. Use Prisma's atomic `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteMany retryCount branch is not scoped to SMS reminders

The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` call has no `method` (or `scheduled: false`) constraint, while the other branch is correctly scoped to `WorkflowMethods.SMS`. `retryCount` is a column on every WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), so the SMS cron will permanently delete email/WhatsApp reminders as soon as anything else increments their retry counter, and it will also delete rows that have already been successfully scheduled (referenceId set) but happened to accumulate retries, losing the ability to later cancel the external job. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`) to that branch.

false_positives.candidate:
No retry counting when message or sendTo is missing, so those reminders still loop forever

`retryCount` is only incremented inside the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` block or in the catch. Reminders that have no `sendTo` (e.g. missing/blank attendee phone number) or an empty rendered message silently fall through every cron run with `scheduled: false` and `retryCount: 0`, and are re-processed on every invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. The same applies to the `continue` at line 68-70 when `workflowStep`/`booking` is null. The stated goal of the PR (stop endlessly reprocessing unschedulable reminders) is therefore only partially achieved.

No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour

The PR introduces new deletion semantics (drop reminders once retryCount > 1) and new increment paths (scheduleSMS returning falsy, and thrown errors), but no unit/integration test is added. Regressions such as deleting reminders of the wrong method or never incrementing the counter would not be caught; a test asserting retryCount increments on failure, that a reminder is removed after the second failure, and that non-SMS reminders are untouched would protect this logic.

OR-ed delete predicate on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder

The delete condition is now `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. `retryCount` has no index and the OR prevents the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index from satisfying the whole predicate, so Postgres will likely sequentially scan the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron run. On a large table this makes the cron noticeably slower and takes row locks broadly; consider issuing two separate scoped deletes or adding an index covering the retry condition.

Prisma update inside catch can throw and abort processing of remaining reminders

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the catch block is not itself guarded. If that write fails (connection error, row deleted concurrently by the deleteMany above — P2025 record not found), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop and out of `handler`, so all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the `{ message: "SMS scheduled" }` response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Caching tests deleted while the memoization code remains

The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` was removed, but the service still memoizes both (`getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`, insightsBooking.ts lines 83-95). The memoization has a subtle contract (`undefined` means "not computed", `null` is a valid cached filter result); with the tests gone, a regression such as recomputing on every call or treating a cached `null` as uncached would go unnoticed. Port the caching assertions to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations instead of dropping them.

New `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` loses discriminated-union type safety and silently denies access

The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`) instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with no `teamId` and it compiles; at runtime `safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and every query silently returns `1=0` (no rows) with no error or log. Previously this was a compile-time error. Keep the discriminated union in the constructor signature, or at least surface the validation failure (throw/log) instead of degrading to an empty result set.

Only user-scope SQL is ever executed against the database; team/org raw SQL is untested

The only test that runs real SQL (`$queryRaw ... WHERE ${baseConditions}`) uses `scope: "user"`, which exercises only `"userId"`, `"teamId"`, `"eventTypeId"` and `"eventParentId"`. The team/org conditions, which are the newly hand-written SQL most likely to be wrong (quoted column `"isTeamBooking"`, and `= ANY(${array})` array-parameter binding), are only compared string-wise against hand-copied `Prisma.sql` literals. A misspelled/renamed view column or an array binding the driver rejects would pass all tests and fail in production. Add at least one `$queryRaw` execution for team scope and one for org scope asserting the expected booking ids.

Org/team scope expectations depend on undefined DB row ordering

The expected SQL parameters are arrays in a fixed order (`[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`), but these come from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which issue no `ORDER BY`. `toEqual` on arrays is order-sensitive, so this test can fail intermittently depending on Postgres row ordering. Sort the ids before comparing (or compare as sets).

Public `findMany()` removed without updating any callers

`InsightsBookingService.findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`. This is a breaking change to the service's public surface: any consumer that previously did `service.findMany({ select: ... })` (the old integration test did exactly that) will now fail to compile/run. This PR only touches the service and its test, so if any production code path (insights routers/handlers) calls `findMany`, the build breaks. Either keep a `findMany` wrapper that executes `$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()`, or update all call sites in this PR.

Public condition getters return unparenthesized composite SQL (operator-precedence hazard)

`buildFilterConditions` returns the single-condition case verbatim, e.g. `"eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions`/`buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` similarly return top-level `AND`/`OR` expressions with no surrounding parentheses (see also lines 135, 164, 197). `getBaseConditions` happens to wrap them, but these are public async methods (`getAuthorizationConditions`, `getFilterConditions`) and any caller doing `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filters}` or `WHERE ${base} AND "startTime" > $x` will get silently wrong results because `OR` binds looser than `AND` — in the authorization case that means returning bookings the user is not allowed to see. Wrap each produced fragment in parentheses at construction time.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dev script is macOS-only and writes to a path outside the repo

`sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on Linux (GNU sed) the empty string is interpreted as the script argument and the command fails with "unknown command", leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged while the script still prints the success message. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` in the repo's parent directory rather than the project one. Resolve the path relative to the script location and use a portable in-place edit.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError

The handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps unknown errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) and, in production, replaces the message, so the client cannot distinguish "not yours" from a server failure, and the failure is logged/reported as a server bug. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` as the other handlers in this router do.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting

`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale and 12h/24h time preference, so a non-US user sees MM/DD/YY and AM/PM dates inside an otherwise translated string. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()`) / the existing date-formatting helpers instead of a literal "en-US".

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache deletion only supports personal credentials, not team/delegation credentials

Access is validated with `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Calendar credentials installed on a team have `userId = null`, and delegation credentials are in-memory with negative ids, so for those connected calendars the lookup fails and the mutation errors out. The new dropdown in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper renders the "Delete cached data" entry for any credential that has a cache row (including team/delegation-backed ones), so users will get an "Error deleting cache" toast with no way to clear the cache. Either extend the authorization check (team membership / delegation ownership) or hide the action for those credentials.

Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature check

The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` request performs an extra `groupBy` on CalendarCache even for users/teams without calendar cache enabled, and stale rows left over from a previously enabled feature are surfaced in the UI as an active cache (with a delete action) even though caching is off.

Migration backfills updatedAt with NOW(), making stale caches look fresh

All pre-existing CalendarCache rows get `updatedAt = <migration time>`. The new UI reads this value and renders "Last updated: <timestamp>", so immediately after deploy every existing cache — including ones written weeks ago — appears to have been refreshed at deploy time. Consider backfilling from a better proxy (e.g. `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`) or making the column nullable so "unknown" can be shown. Also the auto-generated warning block ("Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value") contradicts the statement actually executed, which does specify a default.

No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds

This PR adds a destructive mutation (`viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) with hand-rolled authorization and a new repository read (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), but no unit tests. At minimum there should be tests asserting that (a) a credential belonging to another user cannot have its cache deleted, (b) the matching CalendarCache rows are removed for an owned credential, and (c) the status aggregation returns the max updatedAt per credentialId and an empty result for unknown ids.

Unnecessary blanket UPDATE of all SelectedCalendars on every cache fill

`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an `UPDATE "SelectedCalendar" SET "updatedAt" = now() WHERE credentialId = ?` for every credential each time availability is cached (including on every Google webhook). The PR description itself states `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache), so this is a write with no reader that adds row churn and lock contention on a hot path. For delegation credentials (negative in-memory id) it also matches nothing. Remove it or document a concrete consumer.

UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that the function never uses

`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but neither field is read anywhere in this file. Because `UserWithCalendars` is the public input type of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (also re-exported as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` for `@calcom/platform-libraries`), every external caller that selects only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` now fails type-checking and must be updated (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated in this PR). Revert the widening unless the fields are actually needed.

deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query

The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. `onSuccess` is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and undefined on several call sites of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper. In that case the success toast is shown but the UI keeps displaying the old "Cache Status / Last updated" entry until a manual refresh, making it look like deletion failed. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the mutation's onSettled/onSuccess.

dev:cron depends on tsx which is not a declared dependency

`dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not in dependencies/devDependencies, so `npx` will attempt an interactive network install on each fresh environment (and fail in offline/CI contexts), while the now-unused `ts-node` devDependency remains. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it without `npx`.

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt

The query filters only on `credentialId in (...)`, so expired cache rows (`expiresAt < now()`) are reported with their `_max(updatedAt)`. The UI then shows "Cache Status – Last updated: …" for a cache that will never be served, misleading the user about whether the credential is actually cached. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or expose expiry so the UI can label stale caches).

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reminder cancellation promises are no longer awaited

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked fire-and-forget inside `forEach`. Previously the DB work for reminders was part of `prismaPromises` and therefore awaited before the handler returned. Now the handler can return (and in a serverless/edge deployment the invocation can be frozen or torn down) before the `workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` / Twilio cancel + row delete have completed, in which case the reminder is never marked cancelled and the workflow email/SMS is still sent – exactly the bug being fixed. Rejections are also unobserved (unhandled promise rejections). Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (line 488) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` (line 966).

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete path re-introduces the pending-cancellation accumulation and leaks reminder rows

When `immediateDelete` is true the function issues the SendGrid `scheduled_sends` cancel immediately and returns without touching the `workflowReminder` row. Two problems: (1) the row stays in the DB with `scheduled: true` and its `referenceId`, so it is neither deleted nor flagged – it lingers until the generic `deleteMany` in the CRON removes it after `scheduledDate` passes, and it can be "cancelled" again by later code paths; (2) this path is used for the two most common operations – rescheduling (`handleNewBooking.ts` line 968) and workflow/step deletion (`workflows.tsx` lines 214 and 521) – which means those cancellations still pile up as pending cancellations in SendGrid (the 100-pending limit described in the PR description) and will again start failing silently, so cancelled emails will still be delivered. These paths should use the same deferred `cancelled` flag mechanism as booking cancellation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancellation window can be too late for SendGrid's cancellation deadline

Cancellation is deferred to this CRON, which (per the PR description) runs every 15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. SendGrid only honours a cancel request if it arrives sufficiently ahead of the send time (documented as at least 10 minutes). If a booking is cancelled shortly after a CRON run and its reminder is due in ~15–25 minutes, the next run can reach SendGrid with less than 10 minutes to spare and the cancellation is rejected, so the reminder for the cancelled booking is still delivered. Consider cancelling immediately (or on a much tighter schedule) for reminders due within the next hour, or widening/short-circuiting the window.

One failing cancellation aborts the whole cancellation batch and leaves DB rows untouched forever

The whole `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop is wrapped in a single try/catch. If any single `client.request(...)` throws (invalid/expired batch id, SendGrid already has the batch in `cancel` status, transient 5xx), the loop is abandoned: all remaining reminders in the batch are never cancelled and their emails get sent. In addition, the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` objects are Prisma lazy promises that only execute when awaited in `Promise.all` at line 74; because the throw happens before that await, none of the already-processed reminders are deleted. On the next CRON run the same reminders are selected again, the same request fails again, and the cancellation pass is permanently stuck. Each reminder needs its own try/catch (and its delete should be awaited/committed per item).

SendGrid client used for cancellation without an API key

The new cancellation block calls `client.request({url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST", ...})` using the singleton exported by `@sendgrid/client`, but this module only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (line 19). `@sendgrid/mail` holds its own internal `Client` instance, so `setApiKey` on it does not configure the imported `client` singleton (compare `emailReminderManager.ts`, which explicitly calls `client.setApiKey(...)`). As a result every cancellation request here is sent unauthenticated and will fail with 401, the error is swallowed by the surrounding catch, and the "cancelled" reminders will still be delivered by SendGrid – i.e. the bug this PR is supposed to fix is not actually fixed in the CRON path. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this file.

Type-only imports moved into a value import, and formatting will fail lint

`PrismaPromise` is a type-only export of `@prisma/client` but is now pulled in through a value import, and the import list `  Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";` is missing the trailing comma required by the repo's prettier config, so `yarn lint`/format checks will fail on this file. Keep `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise } from "@prisma/client";` for the type-only names and run prettier (the large commented-out `testAction` block was also re-indented by this change, adding unrelated diff noise).

remindersToCancel query is missing method/referenceId filters

`prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` does not filter on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` nor on `referenceId: { not: null }`, unlike every other query in this file. Any row that is flagged `cancelled` but has no `referenceId`, or that belongs to a non-email method, is posted to the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint with `batch_id: null`/a Twilio SID, which produces an error that (per the single try/catch above) aborts the whole cancellation pass. Restrict the query to email reminders with a non-null `referenceId`.

try/catch around the reminder cancellation cannot catch anything

The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...) } catch (error) { log.error(...) }` block wraps synchronous `forEach` calls over async functions. Since the returned promises are not awaited, any rejection from `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` escapes this catch as an unhandled rejection, and the log message is never produced. Await the calls (e.g. `await Promise.all(originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.map(...))`) so the error handling actually works and the cancellations complete before the reschedule continues.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Module-level import promises can produce unhandled rejections and crash the process

Each `import("./x")` promise is created at module scope with no attached handler. If any single app module throws while being evaluated (bad/missing app key, failing SDK init, missing optional dependency), the resulting rejection is unhandled because nothing awaits that specific entry unless the app happens to be used. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` this terminates the process, so one broken app takes down the whole server even though no booking uses it. Previously a failing module was at least surfaced synchronously at import time of the specific consumer. Lazily created promises (thunks) or `.catch()` handling is needed.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async callback in forEach: calendar/video cancellations are no longer initiated before the mutation completes

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` returns immediately; the deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls now only start after the `await getCalendar` microtask resolves, i.e. after `requestReschedule` has already sent the reschedule email and possibly returned. Nothing awaits the resulting promises, so failures to delete the old calendar event / video room are swallowed as unhandled rejections and the old events can be left dangling. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... }` with `await`, or collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`.

false_positives.candidate:
Commented-out example entry points at a non-existent directory

The placeholder comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so a developer who uncomments this line to register a new app gets a module-not-found error. It should read `// example: import("./_example"),`.

Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy

The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … at module evaluation time, which immediately kicks off loading of every app package the moment `@calcom/app-store` is imported. The promises are merely stored, so consumers `await` an already-running import. The net effect is that all ~28 app modules (and their transitive deps such as Stripe/Google/Exchange SDKs) are still evaluated on every request path that touches the app store — the stated goal of async/lazy loading is not achieved, and webpack will still fetch every generated chunk. To get real laziness the entries must be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites invoking the thunk.

Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is already awaited

In the recurring branch the credentials are still iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because the callback is async, `apiDeletes.push` runs only after the awaits resolve — long after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at the end of the handler has captured the (still empty) array. So for "cancel all remaining recurring bookings" the external calendar deletions are neither awaited nor error-checked, and failures surface as unhandled rejections. The sibling non-credentialId branch in the same block was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop; this branch should be too.

getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in its `calendar` field, changing its public contract

`getCalendarCredentials` still looks synchronous, but `calendar: getCalendar(credential)` is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is exported and used outside this module, e.g. destination-calendar/connected-calendar flows and the API app) that calls `item.calendar.listCalendars()` or checks `if (!item.calendar)` will now silently see a truthy Promise and break at runtime. Additionally, promises stored on entries that a caller never awaits can reject unobserved. The function should either be made `async` and resolve the calendars with `Promise.all`, or keep the credential list free of promises.

try/catch around forEach with async callback cannot catch failures anymore

Changing the callback to `async` means the surrounding `try { ... } catch { logger.error(...) }` block can never observe an error: the callback returns a promise that is discarded, so any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` escapes as an unhandled promise rejection (process-level crash on modern Node) instead of being logged. The deletions are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent. Replace with a `for...of` loop using `await` inside the try block.

try/catch around forEach with async callback cannot catch failures anymore

Same problem as in the vital reschedule helper: the callback passed to `forEach` is now `async`, so the enclosing `try/catch` will never see errors thrown inside it; rejections from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` become unhandled promise rejections rather than being logged, and the cancellations are not awaited before the function returns. Use a `for...of` loop with `await` inside the try block.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start instead of the slot end

`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` computation on the previous line; `slotEndTime` is never used. As a result the check `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them, so slots that overrun the end of the organizer's availability (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 15 minutes before the schedule ends) are still reported as available.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false

`if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly constructed Dayjs objects by reference, which is never true. The intended check (a zero-length override, i.e. a day marked unavailable) is therefore dead code; such overrides are only handled accidentally by the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)` branch, and a slot exactly at the override instant would be treated as available. Use `.isSame()` on the two values.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override day short-circuits the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
