true_positives.golden_comment: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
true_positives.matched_candidate:
findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups, breaking promise-based callers

When `name` is empty `findMembers` now returns `undefined` instead of the previous `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Callers treat the return value as a promise (`actions.next`/`previous` return it, and `removeMember`/`addMembers` chain off `findMembers`), so for a new, unsaved group any code that calls `.then()` on the result will throw. Return a resolved promise instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify a code path in the function that lacks an explicit value return and therefore returns undefined. The candidate adds the specific empty-name condition and its impact on promise-based callers.

false_positives.candidate:
remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and the user_count counter cache

`group.users.delete(user_id)` deletes the join rows of a `has_many :through` association, whose default deletion strategy is `delete_all` (raw SQL on `group_users`). This skips all `GroupUser` callbacks and the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on `GroupUser#group`, so `groups.user_count` is never decremented and side effects previously performed by `Group#remove` (title / trust-level / primary-group housekeeping) are not run. The result is a permanently wrong member count shown in the admin UI and in the new `members` endpoint's `meta.total`, plus stale user titles. Use `group.remove(user)` with a looked-up `User` record instead. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id performs a `find`, so a stale/bogus `user_id` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (500) instead of a clean error.

create silently drops alias_level

`create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, but the client's `Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) always posts `alias_level` as well. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a new group has that choice silently discarded; the group is created with the default alias level and the admin must save a second time to apply it. Assign `group.alias_level` in `create` the same way `update` does.

update forces visible=false whenever the param is absent

`group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally, so any PUT to `/admin/groups/:id` that does not include `visible` (or sends a JSON boolean `true` rather than the string "true") will set the group to invisible. Since `update` is now the only way to change group attributes, a partial update from any other client silently hides the group. Only assign when the param is present, and accept boolean values.

add_members crashes when usernames is sent as an array

`usernames.split(",")` assumes a String. If a client posts `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` (a perfectly natural encoding, and the shape the old API accepted via `Array(actions[:add])`), `params.require(:usernames)` returns an Array and `split` raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. Normalize with `Array.wrap(...)`/`to_s.split(",")` before iterating.

members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset

`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to the query. Any anonymous visitor can request `?limit=1000000` on a large group and force the server to load and serialize the whole membership (cheap DoS vector), and `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` makes PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT must not be negative" / "OFFSET must not be negative", returning a 500. Clamp both values (e.g. limit between 1 and 100, offset >= 0).

GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed with no spec coverage

The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`. This is a breaking change for any external consumer or plugin hitting the public members endpoint, and no spec was added or updated for the new shape or for the pagination behaviour (spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb is untouched in this PR, so any existing assertion on the array response is now wrong). Add/update specs covering the new payload, the default limit, and the offset handling.

Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 users

`GroupsController#members` now applies a default limit of 50 to every group (previously only automatic groups were paginated), but this template has no pagination controls and the group-members route just calls `model.findMembers()` once. For any group with more than 50 members the public page now shows only the first 50 with no indication that members are missing and no way to load the rest. Either add pagination/infinite scroll here or request the full list for this view.

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validator performs DB writes, so match statistics are double-counted

`validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which mutates and saves the BlockedEmail row (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`). Because this happens inside validation, every call to `valid?`/`save` writes. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, so a single signup attempt runs the validation twice and inflates `match_count` by 2; any other code path that validates a user with a changed email also silently bumps the counter. Side-effect-free validation plus an explicit statistics update (or an idempotent guard) is needed, otherwise the match statistics are unreliable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same underlying issue: the email-blocking check unexpectedly updates and saves match statistics during a read/check operation. The candidate describes double-counting during validation rather than race conditions or misleading naming, but these are consequences of the same side effects.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive, trivially bypassed

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` does an exact match (`where(email: email).first`) against the value supplied by the signup form. Email addresses are not normalized/downcased before User validation (`User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` verbatim and there is no downcasing callback), so a user whose address `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked can sign up with `Bad@Spamclub.com` and pass validation. The stored block rows are also inserted verbatim, so a mixed-case row would never match a lowercase signup. The lookup should normalize both sides (e.g. `Email.downcase`) and the column/index should store normalized values.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same case-sensitive lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block?, which allows blocked users to bypass the block by changing the capitalization of their email address.

false_positives.candidate:
Non-atomic increment of match_count loses updates

`record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write across two statements. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address (the common case for spam waves) will read the same value and overwrite each other, so `match_count` under-reports. Use an atomic update (`increment!`/`update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`). Additionally `record.save` re-runs the uniqueness validation (extra query) and silently returns false if the record is invalid, so a failed statistics update goes unnoticed.

action_type is NOT NULL with no database default

`action_type` is declared `null: false` but has no default; the only default comes from the model's `before_validation :set_defaults`. Any insert that bypasses the model (bulk import of blocked addresses via SQL/COPY, which the spec comments explicitly anticipate, or `insert_all`-style code) will fail with a not-null violation. Add `default: 0` (block) to the column so the DB and model agree.

rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared across instances

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` creates a single array on the class prototype; every instance of CreateAccountController mutates the same array via `pushObject`. If the controller is ever instantiated more than once (or the app is reset in tests), rejected emails leak between instances and are never cleared, so a previously rejected address stays permanently marked invalid for the page lifetime. Initialize it per-instance in `init` (or reset it when the modal is shown).

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`align-items` mixin emits legacy properties that reject the modern keyword values

The mixin blindly maps the argument onto `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`/`center`/`baseline`/`stretch`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`. So `@include align-items(flex-start)` silently produces invalid legacy declarations and the legacy-only engines fall back to the default `stretch`, producing a different layout than intended. Also `-ms-align-items` is not a real property (IE10 uses only `-ms-flex-align`), and `-moz-box-align` is missing even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so Firefox's legacy box path gets no alignment at all.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that -ms-align-items is not a real property and that IE10 uses -ms-flex-align instead, matching the golden issue despite mentioning additional concerns.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`order` mixin mixes 1-based legacy ordinal groups with 0-based `order`

`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1) while the standard `order` property is 0-based (default 0), and `box-ordinal-group: 0` is invalid. As a result `@include order(0)` emits an invalid legacy declaration, and `@include order(1)` makes the element tie with siblings that have no order set in legacy engines, while in modern engines it is placed after them. Any mixin consumer therefore gets different sibling ordering depending on the engine; the legacy value should be `$val + 1`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require 1-based values, so passing $val = 0 produces invalid declarations and incorrect ordering in older browsers. The candidate adds detail and a proposed offset without changing the underlying issue.

`float: right` on small-action button no longer works now that `.small-action` is a flex container

`.small-action` was turned into a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at line 264). Float is ignored on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule at line 309 has no effect anymore and the action button (e.g. undo/delete on small post actions) will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the container needs `justify-content: space-between`). The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead.

Right-alignment of header `.panel` breaks in browsers that only support the legacy box model

`.contents` is now laid out with the `flexbox()` mixin, which also emits the legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks. Those old box-model implementations do not honour `margin-left: auto` for pushing an item to the end of the line, and the previous `float: right` on `.panel` (plus `float: left` on `.title`) was removed in this diff. In any engine that falls back to `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` (old Android/iOS WebKit, Firefox < 22) the header panel with the user icons/search will be rendered left-aligned next to the title instead of right-aligned, i.e. a visibly broken header. Either keep a float fallback or drop the legacy `box` fallbacks from the mixin.

Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

`include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it never guards the attribute

ActiveModel::Serializers only honours conditional methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — including as `null` for every user who has no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that it then also needs to respect the untrusted-attribute rules, see the separate finding).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same primary issue: include_website_name is missing the required '?' suffix, preventing conditional inclusion of website_name. It does not mention the golden comment's additional string-literal mutation concern, but it clearly matches the conditional-method naming bug.

false_positives.candidate:
`website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous viewers

`untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) deliberately hides `website` (among others) when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true — i.e. a trust-level-0 user's profile seen by an anonymous visitor — as a spam mitigation. The new `website_name` attribute is declared as a plain attribute and is therefore always serialized, exposing the host (and, for same-domain cases, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors. The template renders `model.website_name` as the visible text, so the spam URL becomes visible again even though `model.website` is suppressed. `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because the literal is a fresh unfrozen object on each evaluation, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment `# frozen_string_literal: true` is added to this file (or the global frozen-literal option is enabled). `URI("http://Example.com/user").host` returns `"Example.com"` with the original casing, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is normally lowercase. The equality check on line 141 and the sibling-subdomain comparison on line 146 therefore fail for a user who typed their own domain with capitals, and the full path is not shown even though the domains match. Only `URI#path` is appended, dropping query and fragment from the displayed URL

For same-domain websites the display string is `host + URI(...).path`, which silently discards any query string or fragment (e.g. `http://example.com/u?id=1` is shown as `example.com/u`). Since the whole point of this change is to show the complete URL when the domain matches the instance domain, the link text can now differ from the actual `href`. Consider using the request-URI (path + query) or the full URL minus the scheme.

No test coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch, for non-parsable websites, or for the TL0/anonymous case

The three new examples only cover the `==` branch and the `ends_with?` branch. false_positives.candidate:
raw_html cook method stores and renders unsanitized remote HTML

`Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so posts created by `TopicEmbed.import` keep whatever HTML came from the remote source as their `cooked` value. The RSS path (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` -> `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) passes the feed body through with no tag/attribute whitelist at all (only `import_remote` filters tags via ruby-readability), and the resulting `cooked` is emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb as well as in normal topic rendering. A hostile or compromised feed (or an XSS-laden page scraped from the embeddable host) can therefore inject `<script>`/`onerror` payloads that execute for every visitor of the forum. The imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

`post.present?` does not detect a failed PostCreator run

`PostCreator#create` returns the (unsaved) Post object even when creation fails — it raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` internally, which is swallowed, and the returned post has errors and a nil `id`/`topic_id`. `post.present?` is therefore true for failed creations, and the following `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil, ...)` blows up with a NOT NULL/validation error, masking the real failure (e.g. a title that is too long or a rate limit). Check `post.persisted?` (or `post.errors.blank?`) instead, and bail out gracefully otherwise.

`open(url)` used without requiring 'open-uri'

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but topic_embed.rb only requires 'nokogiri'. `open-uri` is only required in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, which is not loaded on the `retrieve_topic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` path (that path only requires 'topic_retriever'/'topic_embed') unless feed polling happens to be enabled. Without open-uri loaded, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a file name and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so on-demand embed retrieval (and the disqus thor task) fails. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. After the substitution `src.sub(/^\/+/, '')` the result becomes `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for any feed that uses protocol-relative references (common for CDN-hosted assets). Protocol-relative URLs should be left alone or prefixed with the scheme only.

Existing embed with a deleted post raises NoMethodError

In the update branch `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted, or a previous import that stored a bogus post_id). `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then fails with a NoMethodError inside a Sidekiq job, and the embed row is never repaired. Guard for a missing post and either recreate the topic or skip.

Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies, the Redis connection fails, or the job is killed between the two calls, the key stays forever with no TTL, so `retrieved_recently?` returns true for that embed_url for the rest of the Redis instance's life and that page's discussion can never be retrieved (the embed iframe is stuck on the loading page). Use `$redis.set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)` (or SETEX) instead.

Full feed poll executed inline during embed retrieval

`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the complete RSS/Atom poll synchronously (HTTP fetch of the feed plus creation/revision of a topic for every item) inside the `retrieve_topic` job each time an unknown embed_url is requested and feed polling is enabled. One cold embed view can therefore trigger a multi-second-to-minute import, and many concurrent unknown URLs will import the feed repeatedly in parallel (no locking), duplicating work and hammering the feed source. Enqueue the poll instead, or guard it with the same throttle used for HTTP retrieval.

`X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value

`ALLOWALL` is not a defined X-Frame-Options directive. Per the HTML spec/most current browsers an unrecognized value is treated as `DENY` (some older browsers ignored it), so setting this can actively prevent the page from being framed — exactly the opposite of the intent — and makes embedding fail on the browsers that follow the spec. To allow framing, delete the header that the default Rails/Discourse middleware set (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`) and, if restriction is wanted, use a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive with the embeddable host.

Loading page is cached for 1 minute but reloads itself after 30 seconds

`discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `render 'loading'` branch. The loading template reloads the iframe after 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so the reload is served from the browser cache and shows the same "Loading Discussion..." page even after the topic has been retrieved; the user waits at least two cycles. Either skip caching (or use a much shorter max-age) when rendering the loading page, or make the reload cache-busting.

Spec stubs TopicView.new to return nil, so the rendered template raises

`TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` has no `returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil. The default `best` template then evaluates `@topic_view.posts.present?`, raising NoMethodError on nil during render, which makes the example (and the assertions in the `after` block) fail rather than verify the success path. The mock needs to return a double exposing `posts`/`topic`, or the spec should use `render_views false` with an explicit template stub.

Editing the existing CreateTopTopics migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that any environment which re-runs this migration (schema reload, `db:migrate:redo`, re-running from a reset schema_migrations) will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and all its rows instead of failing loudly. The thread import was switched to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which drops the previous `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so imported topics are now dated at import time instead of the original Disqus thread date, and the removed `--category` option means imported topics can no longer be placed in a category. The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` with the same path as input and output and never inspects the return value. If `convert`/`ImageOptim` fails (which `convert_with` reports by returning false after swallowing the exception), the destination file — i.e. the user's original upload — may have already been truncated or left partially written, and the loop then runs up to 5 more times on the broken file before the (now corrupt) data is stored via `Upload.create_for`. Convert into a separate temp file and `break` out of the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false, keeping the original intact.

The downsize call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When that setting is false (the default), `OptimizedImage.optimize` uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert #{from}[0] ...` — only the first frame. Because the output path is the uploaded file itself, a large animated GIF uploaded by a user is permanently converted to a single-frame image, losing content the user intended to post. The thumbnail setting is also the wrong switch for deciding how to re-encode an original upload; animation should be preserved regardless (use `allow_animation: true` or a dedicated setting).

The loop gives up after 5 iterations of 80% scaling. If the image is still over `max_image_size_kb` (very likely for e.g. a 40 MB photo with a 1 MB limit, since 5 iterations only reduce area to ~33%), `Upload.create_for` rejects it and the user sees a validation error even though the feature claims uploads are "automatically reduced to allowed size". The HTTP 413 handler now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. A 413 comes from the web server's own body-size limit, which is unrelated to this constant, so the dialog will state a limit that is wrong for most installations and misleads users about what size is acceptable.

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap and is used for every `type`, including non-image attachments which are never downsized afterwards. Sites that configure smaller limits now fetch (and buffer) up to 10 MB from a remote URL before rejecting it, and sites with larger configured limits can no longer use the API URL path for bigger files.

The PR adds a non-trivial in-place image re-encoding loop to `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. false_positives.candidate:
Video booking references no longer store credentialId

In `create()`, `referencesToCreate` now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously the non-calendar branch used `result.credentialId`, i.e. the video credential id returned by `createMeeting`. With this change every `_video` booking reference is persisted with `credentialId = null`. Cancellation code (`handleCancelBooking`: `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`) only deletes the meeting when that id is present, so video meetings will silently never be deleted on cancellation for all new bookings.

updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId

`updateLocation()` builds `referencesToCreate` from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but these results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent()`, which never sets `externalId` or `credentialId` on its returned `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). Both fields are therefore always `undefined`, whereas the previous code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `.credentialId`. The references written by `editLocation.handler.ts` will have no external calendar id or credential id, so subsequent updates/deletes of that booking will target the credential-less legacy path / the "primary" calendar instead of the real destination calendar.

Error diagnostics removed from updateAllCalendarEvents catch block

The catch block still computes the detailed `message` string but the `console.error(message)` call was deleted, so `message` is now dead code and calendar update failures are swallowed completely with no log output. Debugging multi-host calendar failures (the exact scenario this PR targets) becomes impossible; keep a log statement.

deleteEvent destination-calendar fallback can never match

Same inverted predicate as in `updateEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always resolves to `undefined` and `calendarId` degrades to `"primary"`. Events that live in a non-primary destination calendar and whose booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId` will no longer be deleted (Google returns 404, which the handler swallows), leaving orphaned calendar entries.

Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId

`selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined` (when no destination calendar matches `credentialId`); the insert call guards this with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the Meet link into the description does not. When `selectedCalendar` is undefined the patch request is malformed and the event description will be missing the hangout link. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value for the patch.

createEvent now ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId

The target calendar is resolved exclusively via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable and is null for rows created before credential linking, so for those users the event is now written to `"primary"` instead of their configured destination calendar — a behaviour regression from the previous `destinationCalendar.externalId` lookup. Worse, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` still records `externalId: destination.externalId` in the booking reference for the credential-ful branch, so the stored reference can disagree with the calendar actually used, breaking later update/delete.

Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when there is no primary destination calendar

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and the collective handling is `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With optional chaining on `null`, the push is a no-op, so for a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but other hosts do, none of the host calendars are used — exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialise the field to an array (or assign the collected list) instead of relying on `?.push`.

Invalid dynamicUserList surfaces as a 500 instead of 400

`throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is thrown inside the new `try` in `loadUsers`, but the catch only maps `HttpError` and Prisma errors to a 400; everything else becomes `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed client request (empty dynamic user list) is therefore reported as a server error and the actual reason is lost. Throw an `HttpError` with status 400 directly.

organization relation removed from the dynamic-booking user select

In the `!eventTypeId` (dynamic group booking) branch of `loadUsers`, the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` sub-select was dropped. Any downstream consumer of `user.organization` for dynamic bookings (e.g. building org-scoped booker URLs) will now see `undefined`, and the two branches of `loadUsers` return structurally different user shapes, which weakens the inferred type the comment claims to rely on. Re-add the select unless you have verified no consumer reads it.

Recurring cancellation now issues duplicated delete calls per calendar reference

The recurring branch (iterate all of the user's calendar credentials × all `updatedBookings`' first calendar reference) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references on a booking the whole credential×booking deletion matrix is executed N times, sending the same `deleteEvent` request repeatedly to each provider (and pushing N× duplicate promises into `apiDeletes`). For multi-host collective recurring events this multiplies external API calls and the risk of rate limiting. Hoist the recurring handling out of the per-reference loop.

For each destination without a `credentialId`, the code creates an event in every calendar credential of the matching integration type (`this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)`). Now that `destinationCalendar` is an array and is populated with each collective host's calendar, two hosts with credential-less Google destination calendars cause 2 × (number of google credentials) event creations, i.e. duplicate calendar entries for the same booking. Additionally the resulting `EventResult`s carry no `externalId`, so the persisted booking references lose the external calendar id. De-duplicate destinations and pass the destination's `externalId` through.

This PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across ~20 files and adds new branching in `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` (per-destination credential resolution, DB credential fallback, collective host aggregation), yet no unit/integration tests were added and the only test touched is an e2e expectation value. Given the number of null/empty-array edge cases introduced (see the Google Meet crash and the dropped collective calendars), at least tests covering: empty destinationCalendar, destination without credentialId, and a collective event with two hosts, are needed before merge.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Module-level import promises can produce unhandled rejections and crash the process

Each `import("./x")` promise is created at module scope with no attached handler. If any single app module throws while being evaluated (bad/missing app key, failing SDK init, missing optional dependency), the resulting rejection is unhandled because nothing awaits that specific entry unless the app happens to be used. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` this terminates the process, so one broken app takes down the whole server even though no booking uses it. Previously a failing module was at least surfaced synchronously at import time of the specific consumer. Lazily created promises (thunks) or `.catch()` handling is needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify unhandled failures from dynamic imports and recommend catching those failures. The candidate adds detail about module-scope promises and process crashes, but the underlying concern matches the golden comment's request for graceful import-failure handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
try/catch around forEach with async callback cannot catch failures anymore

Changing the callback to `async` means the surrounding `try { ... } catch { logger.error(...) }` block can never observe an error: the callback returns a promise that is discarded, so any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` escapes as an unhandled promise rejection (process-level crash on modern Node) instead of being logged. The deletions are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent. Replace with a `for...of` loop using `await` inside the try block.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify async callbacks passed to forEach whose promises are discarded, leaving deletions unawaited and errors outside the surrounding try/catch. The candidate also describes incomplete sequencing and recommends the same for...of with await fix.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy

The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … at module evaluation time, which immediately kicks off loading of every app package the moment `@calcom/app-store` is imported. The promises are merely stored, so consumers `await` an already-running import. The net effect is that all ~28 app modules (and their transitive deps such as Stripe/Google/Exchange SDKs) are still evaluated on every request path that touches the app store — the stated goal of async/lazy loading is not achieved, and webpack will still fetch every generated chunk. To get real laziness the entries must be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites invoking the thunk.

getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in its `calendar` field, changing its public contract

`getCalendarCredentials` still looks synchronous, but `calendar: getCalendar(credential)` is now a `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is exported and used outside this module, e.g. destination-calendar/connected-calendar flows and the API app) that calls `item.calendar.listCalendars()` or checks `if (!item.calendar)` will now silently see a truthy Promise and break at runtime. Additionally, promises stored on entries that a caller never awaits can reject unobserved. The function should either be made `async` and resolve the calendars with `Promise.all`, or keep the credential list free of promises.

try/catch around forEach with async callback cannot catch failures anymore

Same problem as in the vital reschedule helper: the callback passed to `forEach` is now `async`, so the enclosing `try/catch` will never see errors thrown inside it; rejections from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` become unhandled promise rejections rather than being logged, and the cancellations are not awaited before the function returns. Use a `for...of` loop with `await` inside the try block.

Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is already awaited

In the recurring branch the credentials are still iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because the callback is async, `apiDeletes.push` runs only after the awaits resolve — long after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at the end of the handler has captured the (still empty) array. So for "cancel all remaining recurring bookings" the external calendar deletions are neither awaited nor error-checked, and failures surface as unhandled rejections. The sibling non-credentialId branch in the same block was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop; this branch should be too.

Commented-out example entry points at a non-existent directory

The placeholder comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so a developer who uncomments this line to register a new app gets a module-not-found error. It should read `// example: import("./_example"),`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inconsistent metric tag key and high-cardinality tag value for shard tags

`spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `shard=<comma-joined shard list>` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses the key `shards` for the same value. Dashboards/alerts filtering on `shard` will silently miss `wait_produce`, and a comma-joined value such as `"0,4,8"` is a different tag value for every shard-to-process assignment, which breaks aggregation by shard and inflates metric cardinality whenever partition assignment changes. Pick one key and emit a stable, low-cardinality value (e.g. the process index) or emit per-shard series.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same tag-key inconsistency: produce and segment_size_bytes use 'shard' while wait_produce uses 'shards' for the same shard value, so shard-filtered dashboards miss wait_produce. The extra cardinality concern does not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched

`test_basic` monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at line 15, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") does nothing. The test still relies on the flusher thread having produced the message before `step.join()` returns, so the intended synchronization is absent and the test remains timing-dependent/flaky. Use a real sleep (e.g. `from time import sleep as real_sleep` captured before patching, as `test_flusher.py` does) or poll until `messages` is non-empty.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug in test_basic: time.sleep is monkeypatched to return immediately, so the added time.sleep(0.1) does not actually wait and the intended synchronization is missing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
join() aborts the shutdown loop, leaving the remaining processes unterminated

In `join()`, when the deadline has passed the loop `break`s out before reaching the `process.terminate()` call for the remaining entries of `self.processes`. With more than one flusher process, a timed-out join therefore terminates only the processes iterated before the deadline expired; the rest are left running and continue flushing segments while the consumer is shutting down/rebalancing. (Additionally, `remaining_time` is computed but never used, and the `terminate()` call itself is dead for spawn processes because of the same `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` problem.) Terminate every process unconditionally after the wait loop.

Although the candidate's primary focus is a separate loop-break bug, it does identify the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
join() aborts the shutdown loop, leaving the remaining processes unterminated

In `join()`, when the deadline has passed the loop `break`s out before reaching the `process.terminate()` call for the remaining entries of `self.processes`. With more than one flusher process, a timed-out join therefore terminates only the processes iterated before the deadline expired; the rest are left running and continue flushing segments while the consumer is shutting down/rebalancing. (Additionally, `remaining_time` is computed but never used, and the `terminate()` call itself is dead for spawn processes because of the same `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` problem.) true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same shutdown bug: a deadline-triggered break in join() skips terminate() for remaining flusher processes, leaving them running. The candidate's additional notes do not change the core issue.

false_positives.candidate:
kill() is never called on unhealthy spawn processes (isinstance check is always False)

`_ensure_processes_alive` only kills the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes here are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` derives from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.context.Process` (which is what the module-level `multiprocessing.Process` alias resolves to), so the isinstance check is always False and `kill()` is never invoked. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Consequence: when a flusher is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`) the old process keeps running while a replacement is started for the same shards, so two processes concurrently flush the same Redis shards and produce duplicate/fragmented segments to `buffered-segments`, and leaked processes accumulate on every restart. Use `process.kill()` guarded by `hasattr`/`BaseProcess` instead.

New multi-process flusher test only asserts bookkeeping, never exercises flushing across shards

`test_flusher_processes_limit` creates 4 partitions with `flusher_processes=2` but never submits a message and never asserts that segments from all 4 shards are produced. It only checks `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes` and the total shard count. The behaviour this PR actually changes — several shards being flushed by one worker, and all shards being covered by the shard->process mapping — is untested. Consider submitting spans for each partition and asserting that one produced message per shard arrives, and that `process_to_shards_map` is a partition of `assigned_shards` (no duplicates/omissions).

Dead method `_create_process_for_shard` left behind

`_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called anywhere (restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). Dead code that duplicates restart logic is a maintenance hazard — a future caller would restart a whole process group from a single shard id. Remove it.

Class docstring claims one process per shard and documents a non-existent param

The docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the number of processes is `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))`, and the consumer CLI defaults `--flusher-processes` to 1, so the normal configuration is a single process handling all shards. The docstring also still documents `:param topic:` which is not an argument, and does not document the new `max_processes` argument. This misleads operators about the default parallelism.

A new SpansBuffer (and its Redis clients) is created in the parent on every restart without releasing the old one

`_create_process_for_shards` constructs a fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` and stores it in `self.buffers[process_index]`, overwriting the previous instance. The parent process keeps using these buffers for `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()`, so each unhealthy-process restart (up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per process) leaves the previous buffer's Redis connections unclosed in the parent. Reuse the existing buffer for the process index, or close the old one before replacing it.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error IDs are paired with the wrong nodestore payloads

`fetch_error_details()` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (which returns a mapping keyed by node id and may omit/reorder missing keys), and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Any missing or re-ordered entry shifts the pairing, so an `ErrorEvent` can be created with the id of one error and the title/message/timestamp of another, producing wrong error text and wrong chronological placement in the Seer prompt. Iterate `events.items()` and map the node id back to the original event id instead of zipping the raw `values()`. The surrounding `except Exception: return []` also means this silently degrades to "no errors" rather than surfacing the problem.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi preserves input order, but its mapping may omit or reorder keys, causing error IDs to be paired with the wrong payloads.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics event recorded before feature check and request validation

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is executed as the first statement of `post()`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. Every request from orgs without the feature, and every malformed/polling request, is counted as an assemble event, so the metric does not reflect actual assemble attempts. true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same issue: the candidate list-walk records the event before the user-visible response, so analytics are emitted even when the feature flag later rejects the request. The extra mention of validation does not change the underlying bug.

false_positives.candidate:
get_environment_info triggers a per-issue recommended-event lookup during PR comment generation

`get_environment_info()` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment. That helper performs a search/snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per issue, so generating a comment for the top 5 issues now issues up to 5 extra remote queries inside the webhook/task path that previously only read `issue.culprit` from the already-loaded model. This adds latency and external load to every PR comment, and the broad `except Exception` means failures are invisible apart from an info log. Consider batching the environment lookup (or deriving it from data already fetched for the issue list).

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter only applies while searching

`sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `searchQuery` is empty, so the newly added `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` exclusion (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is only applied once the user types something. In the default (no search) state those attributes are still shown, which is the opposite of the intent and makes the list inconsistent as soon as a user starts/clears a search. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied to the base list, independently of the search term.

Hook can now return undefined attributes where it previously always returned a TagCollection

The hook was rewritten to return `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data` from `useQuery`. `data` is `undefined` whenever the query errors, is disabled (`enabled` false), or has not run, and `previous` is also `undefined` on the first render — whereas the old implementation always derived a concrete `TagCollection` object (`result.data ?? []` reduced into `{}`). Consumers that do `Object.keys(attributes)` or spread the value (e.g. the filter-key sections / search query builder tag collections) will throw on error or while the hook is disabled. Default to `{}` (or make the undefined case explicit for all callers).

Attribute-keys query key omits the organization

`queryKey` is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` only contains item type, attribute type, project ids and the datetime range — the organization slug used to build the request URL is not part of the key. Two organizations with the same project ids/date range would share a cache entry, so attribute keys from one org can be served for another after an org switch within the same session. Include the organization slug (or the full URL) in the query key.

One invalid report rejects the entire batch

The POST handler returns 422 for the whole request as soon as any single report in the array fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same batch. Browsers send reports in batches and will keep retrying the same (permanently invalid) payload, so a single malformed report from one page permanently blocks collection of the rest of that batch. Consider skipping/counting invalid reports and still returning 200 for the valid ones.

Coverage for the application/reports+json content type was removed

The previous test posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"` (the content type browsers actually use for the Reporting API) and asserted the request body was logged. After the refactor every success-path test posts with the default content type, so `BrowserReportsJSONParser` — the only reason the custom parser class exists — is no longer exercised by any test. A regression in the parser media type would silently break real browser reports while the suite stays green.

Diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while reporting a violation The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) scans are independent, so the two regions can overlap and `start + end` can exceed the length of `value` or `sanitized`. `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` then fails with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. A concrete example: value `x

y` sanitized to `x
y` gives start=5, end=5, so `sanitized.substring(5, 1)` throws. Instead of a readable "Illegal HTML in key ..." message the plugin crashes with an unrelated runtime exception, hiding the actual problem. Clamp `end` to `min(len) - start` before building the substrings.

The English counterpart path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, `_<locale>.properties` -> `_en.properties`). If that file does not exist (community-only theme/locale layout, a bundle whose name does not follow the `_xx.properties` convention, or a locale containing digits which the `[a-zA-Z-_]*` class does not match), the constructor throws an unchecked RuntimeException out of `verify()`, which declares `MojoExecutionException`. The Maven run then fails with a raw stack trace rather than a diagnosable plugin error, and the file is not verified. Either skip verification when no reference bundle exists or wrap the failure in MojoExecutionException with the computed path.

Anchor-mismatch error message does not identify the file or key

`messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` omits both the properties file and the message key, unlike the HTML message a few lines below which includes them. `normalizeValue` runs `unescapeHtml4` on the raw property value, so a translation that deliberately contains escaped markup (e.g. `<div>`) becomes real markup before sanitization. The sanitizer strips it and the key is then reported as "Illegal HTML" even though the original value is harmless literal text. This produces false positives that contributors can only work around by rewording the message.

` vs `

` to `

Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian login bundle

`loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian text in the Lithuanian login messages. It replaces the former Lithuanian sentence, so the OTP setup screen for the `lt` locale now shows Italian.

All four tests only assert that a violation is reported. Nothing verifies the negative case: that a bundle whose translation legitimately contains the allowed elements (`br`, `p`, `strong`, `b`), the same anchor as the English source, placeholders such as `{0}`/`{{0}}`, or a `{n,choice,...}` block yields an empty message list. New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations

`getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Any third-party/custom grant type factory compiled against a previous release no longer satisfies the interface and will fail with `AbstractMethodError` (or not compile) once deployed - and because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories and calls `getShortcut()`, the failure happens at server start. Providing a `default` implementation (e.g. deriving a shortcut or returning null and handling it) would keep the SPI backwards compatible.

Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking change

The `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Subclasses outside this repository (and any code that wrapped a Context, e.g. token-exchange contexts) use it; after this change they can no longer compile/link, and there is no replacement that copies an existing Context. If the copy semantics are no longer needed internally, the constructor should still be kept (deprecated) or an equivalent copy path provided.

Context constructor now NPEs on null formParams

The constructor now dereferences `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. Previously `formParams` was only stored, so a null value was tolerated by this constructor. Any caller constructing a Context without form parameters now gets a NullPointerException at construction time instead of later (or never). A null-guard (`formParams == null ? null : formParams.getFirst(...)`) would preserve the previous contract.

Decoding throws IllegalArgumentException for any token id containing ':' in an unexpected format

`getTokenContextFromTokenId` treats any id containing ':' as encoded and then throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the prefix is not exactly 6 characters or if a shortcut is unknown. Token ids produced by a different/older encoder, by a custom `TokenContextEncoderProvider`, or by a federated/externally issued token could legitimately contain ':' and would cause an unhandled runtime exception (HTTP 500) in whatever endpoint decodes the id, instead of degrading to an UNKNOWN context like the no-colon case does. Also the message "Expected length of 6" refers to the prefix, not the token id that is printed, which is confusing.

If a (custom) `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns null, `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantType)` throws NullPointerException; the same happens in `postInit`, failing server startup with an opaque error instead of a message naming the offending factory. In addition, the duplicate-shortcut consistency check performed in `postInit` is not applied on these lazy inserts, so a newly deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites an existing mapping, making decoded grant types wrong.

Session type derived from clientSession.getUserSession() instead of the user session already available

`getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` resolves the user session via `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` and immediately dereferences it. `TokenManager.initToken`, the only caller, already has a non-null `userSession` parameter it uses for exactly the same persistence-state check. Externally visible jti format change without upgrade documentation

Access token `jti` values change from a bare UUID to `<6-char prefix>:<uuid>` (and the same value is reported in the `token_id` event detail). Relying parties, log pipelines and tests that assume `jti` is a UUID (or validate its length/charset) will break. The PR contains no upgrading-guide/release-note entry describing this behaviour change or the new `tokenContextEncoder` SPI.

false_positives.candidate:
Pre-existing local recovery-codes credential is left valid after codes are stored in user storage

`createRecoveryCodesCredential()` calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` and, when the user-storage provider handles it, skips creating/replacing the local credential entirely. Any previously stored *local* recovery-codes credential for that user is neither removed nor overwritten. This is exactly the upgrade scenario this PR targets: a federated user who configured recovery codes before the provider supported the type keeps the old local credential, and `SubjectCredentialManager.isValid()` will still accept those old codes via the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider`. Re-generating recovery codes must invalidate the previous set; here the old codes stay valid indefinitely. Additionally `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now prefers the federated credential, so the stale local credential is invisible in the UI while remaining usable for authentication.

User label and generation timestamp are dropped when codes are stored in user storage

The credential handed to the user-storage provider is built as `new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson)`, i.e. only the raw codes are transferred; the `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (which carries the user-entered label from the `userLabel` form field and the `generatedAt` timestamp) is used only on the local-storage branch. Consequently, for federated users the label the user typed in the required-action form is silently discarded and cannot be shown in the account/admin console. The new value format (a JSON array of raw codes in `getChallengeResponse()` on update, versus a single raw code on validation) is also completely undocumented in the method javadoc, so third-party provider authors cannot implement `updateCredential` for this type correctly.

Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is removed from the wrong store

`getCredential()` can now return a credential coming from the user-storage provider (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`), but when `allCodesUsed()` is true the code still calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only addresses Keycloak's local credential store. For a federated credential this is a no-op (and the id may even be null, since providers typically build the model with `createFromValues(...)` which does not set an id), so the exhausted credential is left in the user storage. Removal/disabling for federated credentials has to go through the provider (`disableCredentialType`), otherwise the stale credential stays reported as configured.

getCredentials() dereferences a possibly null MyUser

`var myUser = getMyUser(user);` is immediately dereferenced (`myUser.recoveryCodes`) without the null check that every other method in this class performs (`isConfiguredFor`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isValid` all handle `null`). `getMyUser()` returns null whenever the username is not in the in-memory map (e.g. a user still cached/linked in Keycloak after being removed from the provider), which turns a credential listing into a NullPointerException propagated to the caller.

Recovery codes cannot be disabled/removed although the type is now reported as supported

`supportsCredentialType()` (line 114) and `isConfiguredFor()` (line 275) were extended for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, but `disableCredentialType()` (line 217) still only handles OTP and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream()` (line 255) only ever reports `CredentialModel.OTP`. As a result, a recovery-codes credential stored in this provider can never be deleted or disabled through the admin/account REST APIs, and the new tests do not cover removal at all (unlike the OTP flows, which have `testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin` / `testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage`). Since this provider doubles as the reference for user-storage credential support, the gap will be copied by implementors.

New test never verifies that a recovery code is consumed/single-use

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` logs in once with code index 0 and asserts the requested code number is 0. Because `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` (line 340) merely checks membership in the stored list and `getCredentials` (line 237) rebuilds the model with `createFromValues`, which marks all codes unused, every login will accept the very same code forever and the prompt will always ask for code #1. The single-use semantics of recovery codes — the core security property of the feature, and the behaviour `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`/`allCodesUsed()` depend on — are therefore neither exercised nor supported by the reference provider. At minimum a second login should assert that the previously used code is rejected and/or that the requested code index advances.

Login in new test is not completed and logout result is ignored

Unlike the sibling OTP test (`testOTPUpdateAndLogin`, which calls `testAppHelper.completeLogin()` before `appPage.assertCurrent()` and wraps logout in `assertTrue(...)`), `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` never calls `completeLogin()` after submitting the recovery code and discards the `testAppHelper.logout()` return value. The code-to-token exchange is thus never performed and a failing logout is silently swallowed, leaving the user session behind and potentially affecting subsequent tests in this class (which all reuse the username "otp1").

false_positives.candidate:
Exit-code contract changed: 4 no longer means "recreate required"

`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. These constants are the documented, scriptable contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` (the guide explicitly tells users to rely only on the exit code). Any existing consumer that hardcodes 4 as "recreate upgrade needed" – including automation pipelines and any operator/job code that inspects the terminated container's exit code – will now silently interpret "the rolling-updates feature is disabled" as "perform a recreate upgrade", and will no longer recognise a real recreate result (3). No non-documentation consumer was updated in this PR; please confirm every reader of these codes uses the constants, and consider picking an unused code (e.g. 5) for the new condition instead of recycling 4.

Documented update-compatibility command appends --features, overriding the user's feature set

The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders every command in the Update Compatibility guide as `bin/kc.sh update-compatibility <sub> ... --features=rolling-updates`. `--features` is a single, replacing list, not additive, so a user who copies this command loses all other features they have configured (via `KC_FEATURES`, keycloak.conf or the image build). Since the guide simultaneously warns that "omitting any configuration options will result in incomplete metadata", the documented command produces metadata for a different feature set than the running deployment. In addition, `features` is a build-time option, so for an optimized distribution/image passing it on the CLI is rejected or forces re-augmentation. The guide should instruct users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list (or enable it at build time) rather than show a bare `--features=rolling-updates`.

New FEATURE_DISABLED exit code is not covered by tests

`testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr text and only for the `metadata` subcommand. The newly introduced exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), which is now part of the documented contract and which also collides with the previous meaning of exit code 4 (recreate upgrade), is never asserted; neither is the feature-disabled path of the `check` subcommand. Also no test asserts the new recreate exit code 3. A future renumbering or a regression in the feature gate would not be caught. Add assertions on `exitCode()` for both subcommands with the feature disabled, and for the recreate result.

Operator CAUTION about required feature is overbroad/ambiguous

The new CAUTION states unconditionally that "the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." That contradicts the behaviour exercised by `UpgradeTest`, which enables the feature only when `spec.update.strategy` is set and still runs successfully (default/unset strategy) without the feature. As written, readers will think the feature is mandatory for every Keycloak CR managed by the Operator. The text should state precisely when the feature is required (e.g. only when `spec.update` is used) and what "fail" means (CR in error status, reconciliation error).

Test replaces instead of appending the CR's enabled features

`setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` unconditionally overwrites whatever `spec.features.enabled` the base test deployment provides. If the shared test CR template ever enables another feature, it is silently dropped here and the test would exercise a different configuration than intended (or fail for an unrelated reason). The existing list should be read and extended with `rolling-updates`.

`getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. For the newly added `Clients` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (only name=clientId-UUID and owner are set). `requireView()` (line 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" / "...if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails, like the other `require*` methods in this interface. The docs should state the throwing behaviour, otherwise implementers/callers are misled about the contract.

The PR adds the scopes `configure`, `map-roles`, `map-roles-composite`, `map-roles-client-scope` and the client-scope related evaluations (`canManage(ClientScopeModel)`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)`, `canManageClientScopes()`), but the new tests only cover MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. `canMapClientScopeRoles` / `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and the ClientScopeModel-based checks have no coverage, so regressions in those code paths (including the ones that intentionally differ from V1) would go unnoticed.

The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `true` when the caller has either `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` **or** `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource. `canManage()` (no argument) is the check behind `GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManage()`, which `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` uses to authorize group creation. Consequently an admin granted only a read-only `view` permission on `Groups` can create top-level groups, a privilege escalation. true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authorization Resource IDs instead of group IDs

Group resources in the FGAP v2 schema are stored with `name == group.getId()` (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource.getId()` is a separate generated UUID. This method (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, and `hasPermission` resolves the argument via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so the lookup always misses and the evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource — per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are therefore never detected here; and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, whereas callers (`UsersResource.searchForUser` via `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`, and `UsersResource.getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`) expect group IDs and match them against group membership. Result: `GET /users/count` returns 0 (or wrong values) for an admin whose only visibility comes from group `view-members` permissions, inconsistent with `GET /users`, and the group-id filter pushed into the user query can never match. The V1 implementation correctly uses `resource.getName()`. Note also that `findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` returns the all-groups resource itself, whose name is `"Groups"` and is not a group ID, so it would be added to the set as a bogus group ID if an all-groups permission exists.

This causes per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS checks to miss and fall back to the all-groups resource, producing incorrect group filtering and counts.

In `hasPermission`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns `null` if the realm does not support the authorization schema (e.g. `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() == false`) or if the `Groups` resource does not exist (realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change). The returned value is used without a null check in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()`, producing an NPE / HTTP 500 on ordinary admin endpoints (group listing, user search) instead of a clean `false`. Note `MgmtPermissionsV2` is selected purely on the `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature flag, so a realm with the feature on but admin permissions turned off (while the admin-permissions client still exists) reaches this path.

`AdminPermissions.registerListener` only registers the `GroupRemovedEvent` handler when the v1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature is enabled, and `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` anyway. Beyond growing stale data, these orphan entries show up when listing permissions/resources in the admin API (where `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` cannot resolve them) and must be deleted manually. A removal hook (analogous to the v1 listener) should delete the group resource and its permissions.

`getResourceName` resolves friendly names only for `USERS` ("All users" / username). With `GROUPS` now a supported resource type, permissions created for a group resource fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (created with name only). As a result the admin API/console shows `null` instead of the group name (or "All groups") for group-scoped permissions, which is the exact problem the Users branch was added to solve.

`init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so realms that already enabled FGAP v2 before this change keep an admin-permissions client without the `Groups` resource and without the new `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, `view-members` scopes. In such realms creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (the scope lookup at line 125 returns null) and `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` gets a null all-groups resource. Either a migration that adds the missing resource/scopes or lazy creation is needed.

The new `switch (resourceType)` dereferences `resourceType`; a `null` value now produces an NPE (HTTP 500) whereas the previous `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` chain fell through to the explicit `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ...")`. `getOrCreateResource` is reachable for policy representations other than `ScopePermissionRepresentation` (which is the only type validated by `throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided`), so a request without `resourceType` can hit this. `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` (and the same change in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`) no longer computes the realm-wide `canView()` once. With `GroupPermissionsV2`, each group in the page triggers `resourceStore.findByName`, `getResourceTypeResource`, `policyStore.findByResource` and a full policy evaluation — i.e. several DB round trips and an authz evaluation per group even for an admin holding a single all-groups `view` permission. For realms with many groups this is a measurable regression on group listing; the previous code evaluated the global permission once and skipped per-item evaluation.

`registerListener` now evaluates `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` once, when the provider event listener is registered during factory initialization, instead of on each event. If the profile is not yet fully resolved at registration time (or registration happens before feature configuration), the listener is never registered and role/client/group permission cleanup on removal silently stops working for the whole server lifetime, with no error. Keeping the check inside `onEvent` (or asserting profile availability at registration) avoids this ordering dependency.

Javadoc on requireManageMembers / getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is wrong

The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` — a copy/paste error that misleads implementors of the interface. Additionally `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a `Set<String>`.

`public static Stream<GroupModel> searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` is deleted outright. Although it lives in `server-spi-private`, that module is compiled against by custom providers; any extension calling this helper will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` after upgrade. If removal is intended, deprecate-and-delegate (or at least note the removal in upgrade docs) rather than removing in the same release.

`readLength()` returns `-1` for the indefinite-length form (0x80), but callers do not handle it: `readInteger()` passes it directly to `read(length)`, which does `new byte[-1]` and throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException`. Since this decoder parses attacker-controlled DER signature bytes, malformed input escapes as an unchecked exception rather than the declared `IOException` (and in `readSequence()` an indefinite length silently yields an empty list). true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
